meta.note: Thursday morning briefing. Three top stories: Vertiv Q3 sales +61%, organic orders doubling, full-year guidance raised by US$0.65 billion; LG AI cooling orders up KRW 2.4 trillion in one quarter, plus KRW 220 billion capacity expansion; cost deadlines arriving within 1–3 days (Oct 30: 50% additional tariff on Canadian air conditioners; Oct 31: Resideo; Nov 1: Siemens DI and Prysmian cables). Earnings window: Carrier/Trane report pre-market tonight, Midea board meeting today. Tariff check: no new finalized policy; the port-fee extension is still a proposal (comments due Oct 30); 178 exclusions and the port-fee pause both expire Nov 9. Event library: 5 new events (Vertiv Q3, UIG close, LG orders of KRW 3 trillion, Daikin Phoenix expansion, Prysmian cable price hike) and 2 new timeline entries (MLCC, copper & aluminum). Tier B batch 11: 1 hit (Prysmian cables).

hotspot_events.title: Vertiv Q3 Sales +61%, Organic Orders Double, Full-Year Guidance Raised by US$0.65 Billion
hotspot_events.heat_reason: The data-center power and cooling leader doubled orders and still guides Q4 organic growth of 50%, pointing directly to a further narrowing CDU/power-distribution/heat-exchange production scheduling window
hotspot_events.summary: Vertiv Q3 net sales of US$4.313 billion, up 61% year on year (organic +55%); adjusted EPS of US$2.21, up 78%; organic orders up more than 100% year on year; adjusted operating margin of 25.2% (+290 basis points); full-year guidance midpoint raised by US$0.65 billion to US$14.65 billion, with Q4 guidance of 50% organic growth.

hotspot_events.title: LG AI Data-Center Cooling Orders Jump KRW 2.4 Trillion in a Quarter, Plus KRW 220 Billion Capacity Expansion
hotspot_events.heat_reason: A rarely seen single-quarter order surge for Korean chillers/CDUs, paired with a US plant build-out, is changing the North American AI-project chiller and large-capacity CDU supply landscape and lead-time negotiations
hotspot_events.summary: LG AI data-center cooling cumulative orders rose from about KRW 0.6 trillion at end-H1 to over KRW 3 trillion at end-Q3, including a long-term chiller supply agreement with North America's Air Control Concepts; LG added KRW 220 billion of capacity expansion (including a new US production base), with its 1MW and 2.6MW CDUs recognized by NVIDIA and the 2.6MW model earning DSX Ready certification.

hotspot_events.title: Cost Deadlines Arrive Within 1–3 Days: 50% Additional Tariff on Canadian Air Conditioners, Resideo, Siemens DI and Prysmian Cable Price Moves in Sync
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Four unrelated cost deadlines fall within 1–3 days; missing one means settling at the new price, and Nov 9 brings a double Section 301 expiry after that
hotspot_events.summary: Oct 30: Canadian-origin air conditioners join the 50% additional tariff; Oct 31: Resideo air zoning product price adjustment; Nov 1: Siemens DI China price adjustment and Prysmian utility cables +5%–7% take effect together; Nov 9: Section 301 exclusions and the port-fee pause both expire.

industry_updates.title: Vertiv Q3 Beats Big and Raises Full-Year Guidance
industry_updates.detail: Q3 net sales of US$4.313 billion, up 61% year on year (organic +55%); adjusted EPS of US$2.21, up 78% (consensus US$1.82); organic orders up more than 100% year on year; full-year guidance midpoint raised by US$0.65 billion to US$14.65 billion; adjusted EPS guidance of US$7.10–7.20; Q4 guidance midpoint of US$4.413 billion in net sales, organic +50%.
industry_updates.source: Vertiv official earnings release via PR Newswire

industry_updates.title: Vertiv Closes Acquisition of Microgrid Company UIG
industry_updates.detail: Closed the acquisition of Utility Innovation Group for about US$1.45 billion in cash, plus up to US$1.15 billion in contingent consideration tied to 12/24-month EBITDA targets; adds microgrid controls, on-site generation dispatch and behind-the-meter power architecture.
industry_updates.source: Vertiv official release via PR Newswire

industry_updates.title: LG AI Data-Center Cooling Orders Surge KRW 2.4 Trillion in a Quarter
industry_updates.detail: Cumulative orders rose from about KRW 0.6 trillion at end-H1 to over KRW 3 trillion at end-Q3, including a long-term chiller supply agreement with North America's Air Control Concepts; LG added KRW 220 billion of capacity expansion (including a new US production base), with its 1MW and 2.6MW CDUs recognized by NVIDIA and the 2.6MW model earning DSX Ready certification.
industry_updates.source: LG Q3 earnings call via Seoul Economic Daily

industry_updates.title: Three Earnings Reports Tonight: Carrier and Trane Pre-Market, Midea Board Reviews Q3
industry_updates.detail: Carrier and Trane both report Q3 pre-market US Eastern Time today (tonight Beijing time); consensus looks for Carrier adjusted EPS of about US$0.81 on revenue of about US$6.08 billion, and Trane EPS of about US$4.74 on revenue of about US$6.5 billion; Midea's board reviews its Q3 report today.

industry_updates.title: Daikin US Modular Plant Capacity Expands to About 2.5x
industry_updates.detail: Daikin Applied's Phoenix Modular Solutions plant grows from 58,000 sq ft to 191,000 sq ft, lifting custom factory-prefabricated hydronic and electrical system capacity by about 150%, with in-plant integration of Daikin's own technology and testing.

industry_updates.title: HEXONIC Offers CDU Heat-Exchanger Selection Support
industry_updates.detail: Provides selection technical support for the liquid-to-liquid heat-exchange interface of data-center CDUs, covering heat capacity, temperature, flow, pressure drop and coolant compatibility, across gasketed plate-and-frame, brazed-plate and shell-and-tube heat exchangers.
industry_updates.source: HEXONIC company release via Access Newswire

siphon_effects.change: Samsung Electro-Mechanics high-capacitance 47μF MLCC rose from US$17.50/100 pcs in August to US$21.60 in October, about +23% (Financial Post citing TrendForce); DigiKey channel lead times of 61 weeks for some Samsung Electro-Mechanics part numbers, 30–52 weeks for Yageo mainstream parts; Emerald's standard-part gauge still steady at 8–12 weeks.
siphon_effects.source: Financial Post citing TrendForce / Newspim / Emerald Q4 update

siphon_effects.change: TrendForce gauge: DRAM lead times of 20 weeks and NAND of 16 weeks continue; Sourceability Q3 gauge: some Micron technologies reach 52 weeks, enterprise SSDs from multiple vendors on allocation with 24–52-week lead times trending longer.

Emerald Q4 gauge: high-performance MCUs and dedicated PMICs at 22–28+ weeks and lengthening; MOSFETs and high-voltage power discrete devices approaching 26 weeks; no new letters from Infineon/onsemi; A2 Global Q4 warning continues.

SMM Oct 28 morning-meeting gauge: LME 3M copper at US$14,621/ton, up about 2.0% from yesterday's morning-briefing gauge of US$14,338/ton; North American scrap copper mainstream grades +11 US cents/lb on Oct 27.
SMM Oct 28 morning-meeting gauge: LME 3M aluminum at US$3,250/ton, up about 5.3% from yesterday's morning-briefing gauge of US$3,085/ton.

cross_industry.key_data: LG Innotek Q3 record sales of about KRW 6.36 trillion but net profit down 25.8% year on year and operating profit down 53.4%; the company attributed it to high-priced raw materials bought while the dollar was strong, compounded by a stronger won at shipment
cross_industry.chain: The combined raw-material and currency squeeze is now materializing in buy-material-heavy manufacturing; quote validity periods should be shortened and price-change clauses moved up front
cross_industry.source: LG Innotek Q3 report via Particle News

cross_industry.key_data: North American scrap copper mainstream grades +11 US cents/lb on Oct 27, brass/bronze +3 US cents/lb, aluminum scrap generally +1–2 US cents/lb
cross_industry.chain: The copper price rise has transmitted from the futures market to spot and scrap; repricing-letter risk is rising for copper tube/copper parts suppliers — confirm the copper price reference date in writing before ordering

supplier_updates.detail: Samsung Electro-Mechanics high-capacitance 47μF MLCC up about +23% from August to October to US$21.60/100 pcs; DigiKey channel lead times of 61 weeks for some part numbers, Yageo mainstream parts 30–52 weeks; standard parts steady at 8–12 weeks.

Prysmian North America announced utility cable products up 5%–7% from Nov 1, citing continued sharp increases in key raw-material costs; the exact increase varies by cable design specification.
Nexans cable capacity bottleneck continues; PCIe 6.0/CXL connector lead times of 36 weeks continue.

No new quotes; carrying the Oct 21 gauge: R22 ex-works at RMB 19,500/ton leading declines; R32 and R134a steady at RMB 65,000/ton each; Gen-3 quotas of 797,800 tons, with the top six producers holding over 90%.
No new price-hike letters (Embraco Oct 19 effective date continues).
Resideo-Honeywell Home air zoning products adjust prices Oct 31 (2 days to go); all other October list items have already taken effect.

SMM Oct 28 morning meeting: LME 3M copper at US$14,621/ton, up about 2.0% from yesterday's gauge; North American scrap copper mainstream grades +11 US cents/lb on Oct 27; no standalone parts price-hike letter.
SMM Oct 28 morning meeting: LME 3M aluminum at US$3,250/ton, up about 5.3% from yesterday's gauge of US$3,085/ton.
Batch 11: 1 substantive hit — Cables (Prysmian utility cables +5%–7% from Nov 1); quick checks of the other 10 categories found no new substantive developments.

warnings.title: Canadian-Origin Air Conditioners Join 50% Additional Tariff from Oct 30 (1 Day to Go)
warnings.action: Complete entry or reroute in-transit Canada-related orders before Oct 30; verify origin and HTS codes

warnings.title: Resideo-Honeywell Home Air Zoning Products Adjust Prices Oct 31 (2 Days to Go)
warnings.impact: North America air zoning product procurement

warnings.title: Siemens DI China Price Adjustment Takes Effect Nov 1 (3 Days to Go)
Prysmian Utility Cables +5%–7% from Nov 1 (3 Days to Go)
warnings.action: Complete orders before Nov 1, or confirm old-price protection in writing and the specification-specific increase

warnings.title: Section 301 Exclusions and Port-Fee Pause Both Expire Nov 9 (11 Days to Go)
warnings.impact: US-related import customs clearance and vessel schedules
warnings.action: Check with your customs broker this week whether HTS lines include 9903.88.69/70; the port-fee extension is only a proposal (comments due Oct 30) — do not schedule vessel space or quotes as if the extension were already in place

warnings.title: Vertiv Orders Double + LG Orders Up KRW 2.4 Trillion in a Quarter
warnings.action: Lock CDU/chiller/heat-exchange key capacity early and confirm lead times in writing; for North America projects, prioritize locking chiller + CDU combined capacity

warnings.title: High-Capacitance MLCC +23%, Lead Times 52–61 Weeks
warnings.action: Lock prices / add orders for high-capacitance and critical part numbers immediately; standard parts proceed on normal 8–12-week schedules — do not stockpile at 61-week assumptions

warnings.title: DRAM Lead Times 20 Weeks, NAND 16 Weeks; Enterprise SSDs on Allocation at 24–52 Weeks
warnings.action: Place Q4 memory demand in a single locked order; sign long-term agreements for 2027 volumes to lock quantities

warnings.title: Power Discrete Devices Approaching 26 Weeks; High-Performance MCUs/PMICs at 22–28+ Weeks
warnings.action: Place orders early for part numbers with lead times over 20 weeks and require written delivery commitments; check price-change clauses

warnings.title: Copper at US$14,621/Ton, Aluminum at US$3,250/Ton, Both Rising Again
warnings.impact: Copper parts and aluminum foil/fin procurement
warnings.action: Lock copper parts and aluminum foil/fins in batches by volume and price rather than a single all-in bet; confirm the copper price reference date in writing before ordering
warnings.trigger: Copper and aluminum prices hitting new highs

warnings.title: R32/R134a Holding High at RMB 65,000/Ton; R22 Pulling Back
warnings.action: Lock R32 volumes at the high level without chasing dips; buy R22 as needed, do not stockpile

warnings.title: Carrier/Trane Pre-Market Q3 Tonight, Midea Q3 Report Today
warnings.action: Watch the three reports' data-center order and lead-time statements; adjust lock-in pace immediately if order gauges change; use reported figures, not pre-market expectations, for ordering
